audience: Adult beginners; arithmetic support is taught before use. Child and teen pathways need separate adaptation.
purpose: Separate production curriculum planning. The existing 36 lessons remain calibration material and are not counted as production delivery.
countPolicy: Ranges are planning estimates, not generation quotas. Replace them with distinct measurable lesson objectives before authoring; never pad by reskinning numbers or repeating definitions.
boundaries: General introductory personal finance, not personalized advice
Teach product families and decision criteria, not product rankings or trading tactics
Explain taxes, protections and rights conceptually; verify every jurisdiction-specific fact with current official sources
Specialist investing, business accounting, professional tax preparation and estate drafting belong in separate courses

sources.use: Coverage cross-check across the four adult personal-finance areas; not a copied teaching sequence or imported EU law.
Practical decision and record-keeping task cross-check; US legal procedures are not transferable to other markets.
Mexican topic coverage and starting point for local source verification.
Brazilian financial citizenship and local-source starting point; current rules require specific primary documents.

designStatus: Original proposed decomposition informed by source coverage. Not an official framework, validated pedagogy, approved course or authored lesson graph.

domains.title: Money available for a decision
outcomes: Track received and paid amounts
Separate promised money from available money
Protect existing commitments before another purchase

domains.title: Arithmetic for financial decisions
outcomes: Compare equal units and totals
Calculate shares, percentage changes and rates
Read tables and distinguish stocks from flows

domains.title: Goals and trade-offs
outcomes: Turn a wish into an amount and date
Identify what a choice leaves unfunded
Revise a goal when constraints change

domains.title: Income and work
outcomes: Plan with variable payment amounts and dates
Distinguish gross, deductions and usable pay
Compare work offers using costs, time and benefits

domains.title: Spending patterns and habits
outcomes: Find recurring costs in a spending record
Distinguish a useful purchase from a persuasive offer
Design a small repeatable change without assuming spare income

domains.title: Budgets and cash-flow timing
outcomes: Build a feasible dated plan
Prepare for periodic expenses
Revise allocations after a shortfall or surprise

domains.title: Accounts, records and access
outcomes: Compare account conditions for actual use
Reconcile recorded movements and balances
Distinguish available access from advertised balance

domains.title: Payments and digital access
outcomes: Choose a payment method for timing, cost and reversibility
Check recipient details and payment status
Protect credentials and recover access through verified channels

domains.title: Prices, contracts and purchases
outcomes: Compare total cost rather than headline price
Evaluate discounts, subscriptions and installment offers
Clarify terms before accepting a commitment

domains.title: Saving and financial resilience
outcomes: Separate planned spending from emergency reserves
Match saving access to a deadline
Adapt contributions when income changes

domains.title: Money through time
outcomes: Compare purchasing power across dates
Model simple and compound growth with explicit assumptions
Distinguish nominal results, real results and uncertainty

domains.title: How borrowing works
outcomes: Trace principal, interest, fees and payments
Compare repayment schedules on the same basis
Test affordability without treating approval as advice

domains.title: Using credit products
outcomes: Read a revolving-credit statement
Explain minimum payments and remaining debt
Compare secured, unsecured and installment commitments

domains.title: Debt problems and recovery
outcomes: Build a complete debt inventory
Compare repayment approaches under explicit constraints
Identify reliable help and avoid rescue scams

domains.title: Credit records and borrowing decisions
outcomes: Distinguish a credit record from income or wealth
Identify errors in a sample record
Find official local procedures without assuming universal score rules

domains.title: Risk, insurance and protection
outcomes: Compare retaining and transferring a risk
Read coverage, exclusions, deductibles and limits
Compare premiums and possible out-of-pocket costs

domains.title: Investing foundations
outcomes: Match risk and access to a goal horizon
Distinguish ownership, lending and pooled investments
Explain diversification without promising protection from every loss

domains.title: Investment information and costs
outcomes: Compare costs and uncertain outcomes using equal assumptions
Read a simplified product disclosure
Distinguish evidence, forecasts and guaranteed-return claims

domains.title: Taxes and public financial systems
outcomes: Distinguish withholding, tax owed and refunds in a stated model
Keep records needed for an official process
Locate current local eligibility and filing information

domains.title: Retirement and longer-term needs
outcomes: Model changing long-term needs and uncertain contributions
Distinguish sources of retirement income
Compare access restrictions and costs without recommending a product

domains.title: Housing and transport decisions
outcomes: Compare ongoing and upfront housing costs
Assess total transport ownership costs
Reassess rent, purchase or financing when circumstances change

domains.title: Shared finances and life changes
outcomes: Agree on shared obligations while preserving informed consent
Plan around caregiving, separation or income interruption
Identify documents and professional help needed after major changes

domains.title: Providers, rights and cross-border money
outcomes: Verify a provider and the scope of its protections
Compare remittance cost and exchange-rate effects
Prepare a supported complaint and recognize misleading sustainability claims

domains.title: Integrated financial decisions
outcomes: Revise a whole-household plan after multiple changes
Explain trade-offs across saving, debt and protection
Recognize uncertainty and decide when qualified local help is necessary
